title: CUET General Test Test 12
subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 and 2026 General Test shift analyses (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Theme of the UN international year 2026
questions.question: The United Nations General Assembly has declared 2026 the International Year of the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Woman Farmer
Why: The resolution, adopted in May 2024, recognises the role of women in farming and food production; the FAO leads the observance. 2026 is also the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.
Why not the others: (A) was 2023, proposed by India. (B) was 2024. (D) was 2025.
Key point: Women make up a large share of the farm workforce in developing countries.

questions.sub_topic: Years for an amount at compound interest
questions.question: In how many years will ₹8,000 amount to ₹9,261 at 5% per annum compound interest, compounded annually?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 3 years
Given: 9,261 ÷ 8,000 = 1.157625.
Step 1: (1.05)ⁿ = 1.157625 = (21/20)ⁿ, and 9,261/8,000 = 21³/20³.
Step 2: So n = 3 years.
Common mistake: stopping too early — after 2 years the amount is only 8,000 × 1.1025 = ₹8,820 (option A) — or using simple interest, which needs more than 3 years.

questions.sub_topic: Rule linking two numbers to a result
questions.question:
Find the rule and complete the last line:
3 * 4 = 25
5 * 12 = 169
6 * 8 = ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 100
Answer steps: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25; 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. So 6 * 8 = 36 + 64 = 100.
Why not the others: (A) adds the numbers. (B) multiplies them. (D) squares their sum, which would make 3 * 4 = 49.
Key point: Check a rule on every given line before using it.

questions.sub_topic: Books and their authors
questions.question:
Match the books in List-I with their authors in List-II:

List-I
(A) Ain-i-Akbari
(B) Baburnama
(C) Harshacharita
(D) Rajatarangini

List-II
(I) Banabhatta
(II) Abul Fazl
(III) Kalhana
(IV) Babur
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: Ain-i-Akbari — Abul Fazl, a minister of Akbar (II); Baburnama — Babur's own memoirs, in Turki (IV); Harshacharita — Banabhatta, the court poet of Harshavardhana (I); Rajatarangini — Kalhana, a history of Kashmir (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Abul Fazl and Babur; (B) swaps Banabhatta and Kalhana; (C) swaps Babur and Banabhatta.
Key point: Rajatarangini (12th century) is often called the first true history written in India.

questions.sub_topic: Facing direction after leaving from the back of a house
questions.question: Rahul's house faces east. He comes out of the back door, walks straight for 50 m, turns right and walks another 50 m. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) North
Answer steps: the back of an east-facing house faces west, so he walks west. A right turn from west faces north.
Why not the others: (A) turns left instead of right. (B) leaves out the turn. (C) starts from the front door.
Key point: The back of a house faces opposite to its front.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about magnets
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about magnets:
A. Like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract.
B. A freely hanging bar magnet comes to rest pointing north–south.
C. Cutting a bar magnet in half separates its north pole from its south pole.
D. The Earth behaves like a huge magnet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and D only
Why: A, B and D are correct: a hanging magnet lines up with the Earth's magnetic field, which is how a compass works.
Why not the others: C is wrong: each half becomes a complete magnet with its own north and south poles; a single pole cannot be separated. Options (B) and (C) include C; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: The Earth's magnetic south pole lies near its geographic North Pole.

questions.sub_topic: Percentage of a percentage
questions.question: What is 40% of 25% of 800?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 80
Given: work from the inside out.
Step 1: 25% of 800 = 200.
Step 2: 40% of 200 = 80.
Common mistake: taking only 40% of 800 (320, option A), or adding the percentages (65% of 800 = 520, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Minimum age to be elected President
questions.question: What is the minimum age for a person to be elected President of India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 35 years
Why: Article 58 requires the President to be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.
Why not the others: (B) is the minimum age for the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. (C) is the minimum age for the Rajya Sabha and legislative councils. (D) is not a minimum age for any of these offices.
Key point: The Vice-President must also be at least 35 years old.

questions.sub_topic: Area of a trapezium
questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 10 cm and 16 cm, and the distance between them is 7 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 91 cm²
Given: area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height.
Step 1: = ½ × (10 + 16) × 7.
Step 2: = ½ × 26 × 7 = 91 cm².
Common mistake: forgetting the ½ (182 cm², option A), or using only one parallel side (16 × 7 = 112, option B; 10 × 7 = 70, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Two series interleaved
questions.question: Find the missing number: 2, 15, 4, 12, 6, 9, 8, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 6
Answer steps: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th terms (2, 4, 6, 8) rise by 2; the 2nd, 4th and 6th terms (15, 12, 9) fall by 3. The missing term belongs to the second series: 9 − 3 = 6.
Why not the others: (B) continues the first series. (C) and (D) do not follow either series.
Key point: When a series jumps up and down, split it into alternate terms.

questions.sub_topic: Classical dances and their home states
questions.question:
Match the classical dances in List-I with their home states in List-II:

List-I
(A) Kuchipudi
(B) Odissi
(C) Manipuri
(D) Mohiniyattam

List-II
(I) Kerala
(II) Manipur
(III) Odisha
(IV) Andhra Pradesh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh, named after a village in Krishna district (IV); Odissi — Odisha (III); Manipuri — Manipur (II); Mohiniyattam — Kerala (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Kuchipudi and Odissi; (B) swaps Odissi and Manipuri; (C) swaps Manipuri and Mohiniyattam.
Key point: Kerala is the home of two classical dances, Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

questions.sub_topic: Office held before becoming Vice-President in 2025
questions.question: C. P. Radhakrishnan took the oath as the 15th Vice-President of India on 12 September 2025. Immediately before this, he was the Governor of which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Maharashtra
Why: Radhakrishnan was Governor of Maharashtra from July 2024 until he became Vice-President. President Droupadi Murmu administered his oath at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Why not the others: (A) is his home state, not one he governed. (C) and (D) are other states.
Key point: The Vice-President's term is five years.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Attorney General
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
A. The Attorney General is the highest law officer of the country.
B. The Attorney General is appointed by the President.
C. The Attorney General may speak in Parliament but cannot vote there.
D. The Attorney General must be a member of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B, C and D
C) A, B and C only
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct (Articles 76 and 88).
Why not the others: D is wrong: the Attorney General is not a member of Parliament but must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court. Options (B) and (D) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: At the state level, the matching office is the Advocate General.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on why 1 is not prime
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The number 1 is not a prime number.
Reason (R): A prime number has exactly two different factors — 1 and the number itself.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: both are true. The number 1 has only one factor (itself), so it does not meet the condition in (R). (R) explains (A).
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: The smallest prime is 2, the only even prime.

questions.sub_topic: Example of a direct tax
questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Income tax
Why: A direct tax is paid by the person on whom it is levied and cannot be passed on to someone else. Income tax and corporation tax are direct taxes.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are indirect taxes: they are collected through the price of goods, so the buyer finally bears them.
Key point: Direct taxes are progressive — the rate rises with income.

questions.sub_topic: Assumptions behind a notice to switch off lights
questions.question:
Statement: A notice in an office reads, "Please switch off the lights when you leave the room."
Assumptions:
I. Lights left on in empty rooms waste electricity.
II. The employees never switch off the lights.
options: C) Both I and II are implicit
D) Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Only I is implicit
Answer steps: the notice asks people to save electricity, so it assumes that lights left on waste it (I). It only needs some people to forget; it does not assume that no one ever switches them off, so II is not implicit.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) accept II, which is too extreme. (D) rejects I, the reason for the notice.
Key point: Words like "never" and "always" usually make an assumption too strong.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the LVM3-M6 launch
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
A. ISRO's LVM3-M6 rocket launched the BlueBird Block-2 satellite on 24 December 2025.
B. The satellite belongs to a company from the United States.
C. At about 6,100 kg, it was the heaviest payload LVM3 had placed in low Earth orbit.
D. The rocket was launched from Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) B, C and D only
C) A, B, C and D
D) A, B and C only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: the satellite, built by AST SpaceMobile to provide mobile connectivity directly from space, was a fully commercial launch.
Why not the others: D is wrong: LVM3 launches from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota; Thumba launches only small sounding rockets. Options (B) and (C) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: LVM3 also launched Chandrayaan-3 in 2023.

questions.sub_topic: Sum of primes between 10 and 30
questions.question: What is the sum of all the prime numbers between 10 and 30?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 112
Given: the primes between 10 and 30 are 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 and 29.
Step 1: 11 + 13 + 17 + 19 = 60.
Step 2: 60 + 23 + 29 = 112.
Common mistake: leaving out 11 (101, option B), counting 15 as prime (127, option C), or leaving out 29 (83, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Exponent equation with base 3
questions.question: Find x when 3 raised to the power (2x − 1) equals 243.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 3
Given: 243 = 3⁵.
Step 1: So 2x − 1 = 5.
Step 2: 2x = 6, so x = 3.
Common mistake: forgetting the −1 and solving 2x = 5 (x = 2.5, option A), or taking 243 as 3⁴ (option C).

questions.sub_topic: Share from a ratio of fractions
questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio ½ : ⅓ : ¼. What is B's share?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ₹2,400
Given: multiply each fraction by the LCM of 2, 3 and 4, which is 12.
Step 1: ½ : ⅓ : ¼ = 6 : 4 : 3, with 13 parts in all.
Step 2: B's share = 7,800 × 4/13 = ₹2,400.
Common mistake: sharing equally (₹2,600, option A), or giving A's share (₹3,600, option C) or C's share (₹1,800, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Tank time when one pipe is turned off early
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 minutes and pipe B in 30 minutes. Both are opened together, and A is closed after 6 minutes. How long does it take to fill the tank in all?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 21 minutes
Given: together they fill 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 of the tank per minute.
Step 1: In 6 minutes they fill 6/12 = ½ of the tank.
Step 2: B fills the other half alone in 30 × ½ = 15 minutes. Total = 6 + 15 = 21 minutes.
Common mistake: giving the time with both pipes open throughout (12 minutes, option B), or only B's time for the second half (15 minutes, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Length of a ladder from its angle with the ground
questions.question: A ladder leans against a wall and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Its foot is 4 m from the wall. How long is the ladder?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 8 m
Given: the ladder is the hypotenuse; the distance from the wall (4 m) is the side next to the 60° angle.
Step 1: cos 60° = 4 ÷ length, and cos 60° = ½.
Step 2: Length = 4 ÷ ½ = 8 m.
Common mistake: giving the height the ladder reaches on the wall (4 tan 60° = 4√3 m, option A), or multiplying by cos 60° instead of dividing (2 m, option B).

questions.sub_topic: River called the Sorrow of Bihar
questions.question: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar" because of its frequent floods and changes of course?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Kosi
Why: The Kosi brings down huge loads of silt from the Himalayas, so its bed rises and it often shifts course, flooding wide areas of north Bihar.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are other tributaries of the Ganga in Bihar. (D) was called the "Sorrow of Bengal" before dams were built on it.
Key point: The Kosi has shifted more than 100 km westwards over about 250 years.

questions.sub_topic: Cost price when profit equals loss
questions.question: The profit made by selling an article for ₹450 equals the loss made by selling it for ₹350. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ₹400
Given: 450 − CP = CP − 350.
Step 1: 2 × CP = 800.
Step 2: CP = ₹400.
Common mistake: adding the prices without halving (₹800, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Youngest of four people
questions.question: P is older than Q. R is older than P. S is younger than Q. Who is the youngest?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) S
Answer steps: R > P > Q > S in age, so S is the youngest.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are both older than S. (C) is the oldest.
Key point: Write the people in one line from oldest to youngest.

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism of pencils, erasers and sharpeners
questions.question:
Statements:
Some pencils are erasers.
Some erasers are sharpeners.
Conclusions:
I. Some pencils are sharpeners.
II. All erasers are pencils.
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Neither I nor II follows
Answer steps: the erasers that are pencils and the erasers that are sharpeners may be different erasers, so I does not follow. "Some pencils are erasers" says nothing about all erasers, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) accept I, which is only possible. (B) and (C) accept II, which turns "some" into "all".
Key point: Two "Some" statements never give a definite conclusion.

questions.sub_topic: State of the floating national park
questions.question: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park and the home of the Sangai deer, is in which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Manipur
Why: Keibul Lamjao lies on Loktak Lake in Manipur. Its floating mats of plants and soil, called phumdis, support the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer), the state animal of Manipur.
Why not the others: (A) has Kaziranga and Manas. (B) has Nokrek and Balphakram. (D) has Ntangki.
Key point: Loktak is the largest freshwater lake in north-east India.

questions.sub_topic: Chemical symbol of sodium
questions.question: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Na
Why: The symbol Na comes from "natrium", the Latin name for sodium.
Why not the others: (A) is the symbol for sulphur. (B) and (D) are not symbols of any element.
Key point: Potassium (K, from "kalium") and iron (Fe, from "ferrum") also have symbols from Latin names.

questions.sub_topic: State of the new Navi Mumbai airport
questions.question: The Navi Mumbai International Airport, whose first phase was inaugurated on 8 October 2025, is in which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Maharashtra
Why: The airport at Ulwe, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, is a second airport for the Mumbai region. Its first phase cost about ₹19,650 crore.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are other states; Goa's second airport, at Mopa, opened in 2022.
Key point: The Navi Mumbai airport is described as India's first fully digital airport.

questions.sub_topic: Country that hosted the 2026 Asian Games
questions.question: The 20th Asian Games, held from 19 September to 4 October 2026, were hosted by Aichi and Nagoya in which country?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Japan
Why: Aichi Prefecture and its capital Nagoya, in Japan, hosted the Games. India finished fourth with 85 medals, including 21 gold.
Why not the others: (C) hosted the previous Games at Hangzhou. (B) and (D) have hosted earlier Asian Games.
Key point: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

questions.sub_topic: Five people in a row facing south
questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing south. Q sits at the extreme right end of the row. R sits second to the left of Q. T sits to the immediate right of P. Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) P
Answer steps: facing south, a person's right is towards the west. Number the seats 1 to 5 from west to east. Q (right end) is in seat 1; R, second to Q's left, is in seat 3. T must be one seat west of P, with seats 2, 4 and 5 free; the only pair that fits is T in seat 4 and P in seat 5. S takes seat 2. The left end (east) is seat 5 — P.
Why not the others: (B) Q is at the right end. (C) S is in seat 2. (D) T is in seat 4.
Key point: When people face south, their left and right are the reverse of yours as you look at the map.

questions.sub_topic: Rivers from north to south
questions.question:
Arrange the following rivers from north to south:
A. Narmada
B. Kaveri
C. Tapi
D. Krishna
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, C, D, B
Why: The Narmada flows through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and the Satpuras; the Tapi flows just south of the Satpuras; the Krishna rises in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra and crosses the Deccan; the Kaveri flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in the far south.
Why not the others: (B) puts the Tapi north of the Narmada. (C) puts the Krishna north of the Tapi. (D) puts the Kaveri north of the Krishna.
Key point: The Narmada and the Tapi are the main west-flowing rivers of the peninsula.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on the speed of sound
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sound travels faster in air than in steel.
Reason (R): Sound needs a material medium to travel.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Why: (A) is false: sound travels much faster in steel (about 5,000 m/s) than in air (about 340 m/s), because the particles of a solid are closely packed. (R) is true: sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) accept the false Assertion.
Key point: Sound is fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases.

questions.sub_topic: Course of action when many students fail
questions.question:
Statement: Many students of a school have failed in mathematics this year.
Courses of action:
I. Extra classes in mathematics should be arranged for weak students.
II. Mathematics should be removed from the school syllabus.
options: B) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Only I follows
Answer steps: extra classes address the problem directly and are practical, so I follows. Removing a core subject does not solve the problem and is not practical, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) accept II, which is an extreme step. (D) rejects I, a sensible remedy.
Key point: A course of action should reduce the problem in a practical way.

questions.sub_topic: Chemical compounds and their uses
questions.question:
Match the compounds in List-I with their uses in List-II:

List-I
(A) Slaked lime
(B) Bleaching powder
(C) Washing soda
(D) Baking soda

List-II
(I) Antacid for acidity
(II) Softening hard water
(III) Disinfecting drinking water
(IV) Whitewashing walls
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) reacts with carbon dioxide in the air to form a white coat of calcium carbonate — whitewashing (IV); bleaching powder releases chlorine — disinfecting water (III); washing soda removes calcium and magnesium salts — softening hard water (II); baking soda neutralises acid — antacid (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps slaked lime and bleaching powder; (C) swaps bleaching powder and washing soda; (D) swaps washing soda and baking soda.
Key point: Slaked lime is made by adding water to quicklime (calcium oxide), a reaction that gives off much heat.

questions.sub_topic: Element at the centre of chlorophyll
questions.question: Which element is found at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Magnesium
Why: A magnesium atom sits at the centre of each chlorophyll molecule; plants lacking magnesium have yellowing leaves.
Why not the others: (A) is at the centre of haemoglobin in blood. (C) builds bones and plant cell walls. (D) is part of DNA and ATP.
Key point: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green.

questions.sub_topic: Energy stored in a stretched rubber band
questions.question: What kind of energy is stored in a stretched rubber band?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Potential energy
Why: Stretching the band changes its shape, so it stores energy as elastic potential energy, which turns into kinetic energy when it is released.
Why not the others: (B) is the energy of a moving object. (C) and (D) are not stored by changing an object's shape.
Key point: A wound-up spring in a toy also stores potential energy.

questions.sub_topic: Odd one out among numbers that are prime
questions.question: Three of these numbers share a property that the fourth lacks. Which is the odd one?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 33
Answer steps: 17, 23 and 29 are prime numbers; 33 = 3 × 11 is not.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all prime.
Key point: Check small divisors (2, 3, 5, 7) to test whether a number is prime.

questions.sub_topic: Stages in the life of a butterfly
questions.question:
Arrange the stages in the life of a butterfly in the right order:
A. Pupa
B. Egg
C. Adult
D. Larva
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) B, D, A, C
Why: Egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult. This change of form is called complete metamorphosis.
Why not the others: (B) puts the pupa before the larva. (C) starts with the larva. (D) puts the adult before the pupa.
Key point: Frogs also go through metamorphosis — egg, tadpole, adult.

questions.sub_topic: Organs that remove urea from the blood
questions.question: Which organs remove urea and other wastes from the blood and form urine?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Kidneys
Why: Each kidney has about a million tiny filtering units (nephrons) that remove urea, extra salts and water from the blood as urine.
Why not the others: (A) makes urea but does not remove it from the blood. (C) remove carbon dioxide. (D) makes digestive juice and insulin.
Key point: When the kidneys fail, a dialysis machine filters the blood instead.

questions.sub_topic: Symbols standing for digits
questions.question: In a code, 2 is written as $, 4 as #, 6 as @ and 8 as %. How is the number 6824 written in this code?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) @%$#
Answer steps: 6 → @, 8 → %, 2 → $, 4 → #, giving @%$#.
Why not the others: (A) swaps the codes for 2 and 4. (B) swaps the first two digits. (D) swaps the codes for 8 and 2.
Key point: Replace the digits one at a time, keeping their order.

questions.sub_topic: Boat speed in still water from two trips
questions.question: A boat travels 30 km downstream in 2 hours and 18 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 12 km/h
Given: downstream speed = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 km/h; upstream speed = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.
Step 1: Boat speed = (downstream + upstream) ÷ 2.
Step 2: = (15 + 9) ÷ 2 = 12 km/h.
Common mistake: giving the stream's speed ((15 − 9) ÷ 2 = 3 km/h, option B), or the downstream speed (15 km/h, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Time shown by a slow watch
questions.question: A watch loses 3 minutes every hour. It is set right at 8 a.m. What time will it show when the correct time is 4 p.m. the same day?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 3:36 p.m.
Answer steps: from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 8 hours. The watch loses 8 × 3 = 24 minutes, so it shows 4:00 − 0:24 = 3:36 p.m.
Why not the others: (B) adds the 24 minutes as if the watch gained time. (C) subtracts the loss for only one hour. (D) subtracts 36 minutes, as if 12 hours had passed.
Key point: A slow watch shows a time earlier than the correct time.

questions.sub_topic: Sister-in-law through a brother's marriage
questions.question: P is the brother of Q. Q is married to R. R is the daughter of S. How is R related to P?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Sister-in-law
Answer steps: R is the wife of P's brother Q, so R is P's sister-in-law.
Why not the others: (A) would need R to be P's parent's daughter. (C) would be the mother of P's wife. (D) would be the wife of P's son.
Key point: A brother's wife is a sister-in-law.

questions.sub_topic: City of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 took place in which city?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Amritsar
Why: General Dyer ordered troops to fire on an unarmed crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on Baisakhi day. In protest, Rabindranath Tagore gave up his knighthood.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are other cities of undivided Punjab.
Key point: The Hunter Committee was set up to inquire into the massacre.

Question: On which day did the factory produce the most units in all three shifts together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Friday
Given: daily totals — Monday 600, Tuesday 620, Wednesday 640, Thursday 690, Friday 700.
Step 1: Compare the five totals.
Step 2: Friday's 700 is the highest.
Common mistake: choosing Thursday because it has the highest morning-shift output (280, option B).

Question: What was the average daily output of the morning shift over the five days?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 260
Given: morning shift: 240, 260, 250, 280, 270.
Step 1: Total = 1,300.
Step 2: Average = 1,300 ÷ 5 = 260.
Common mistake: dividing by 4 instead of 5 (325, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Ratio of evening to night output
questions.question:

| Friday | 270 | 250 | 180 |

Question: What is the ratio of the total evening-shift output to the total night-shift output over the five days?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 23 : 16
Given: evening total = 210 + 220 + 230 + 240 + 250 = 1,150; night total = 150 + 140 + 160 + 170 + 180 = 800.
Step 1: 1,150 : 800.
Step 2: Divide by 50: 23 : 16.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the wrong way round (option A), or using the morning total instead of the evening total (1,300 : 800 = 13 : 8, option C).

Question: By what percentage did the factory's total daily output rise from Monday to Friday?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 16⅔%
Given: Monday total 600; Friday total 700.
Step 1: Increase = 100.
Step 2: Percentage increase = 100 ÷ 600 × 100 = 16⅔%.
Common mistake: dividing the increase by Friday's total (100 ÷ 700 ≈ 14.3%, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Good units after defects in each shift
questions.question:

Units produced by a factory in each shift over five days

| Monday | 240 | 210 | 150 |

| Thursday | 280 | 240 | 170 |
| Friday | 270 | 250 | 180 |

Question: On Thursday, 5% of the morning-shift units, 10% of the evening-shift units and 20% of the night-shift units were defective. How many good units were produced on Thursday?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 618
Given: Thursday — morning 280, evening 240, night 170; total 690.
Step 1: Defective = 5% of 280 + 10% of 240 + 20% of 170 = 14 + 24 + 34 = 72.
Step 2: Good units = 690 − 72 = 618.
Common mistake: giving the number of defective units (72, option C), or applying one rate to the whole day (10% gives 621, option B; 20% gives 552, option D).
